title: Predictive GPU Thermal & Capacity Playbook for Private Deploys
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview
========
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's recommended approach for predictive thermal management and capacity planning for on-prem / private GPU nodes running the inference runtime. It consolidates monitoring signals, predictive heuristics, cooling and power controls, and operational runbooks to reduce unexpected throttling, improve inference latency SLO adherence, and extend hardware lifetime.

Scope
-----
- Applies to private deployments using NVIDIA A100, H100, or equivalent GPU nodes managed by the Redwood onprem agent (service name: redwood-agent).
- Targets tenant-facing inference racks and edge appliances that host inference workloads (dedicated pools and multi-tenant on-prem installations).
- Excludes bare-metal provisioning steps (see field-installation guide) and cloud-hosted capacity autoscalers.

Goals and outcomes
------------------
- Prevent thermal throttling that causes latency spikes above the 99th percentile SLO.
- Forecast capacity and thermal headroom 24–72 hours ahead to prepare graceful throttles, tenant notifications, or temporary failovers.
- Reduce unscheduled GPU derates and hardware replacements by 30% year-over-year.

Key metrics and signals
-----------------------
- GPU core temperature (C): nvml.temperature.gpu (Prometheus metric: node_nvml_temperature_celsius)
- GPU power draw (W): nvml.power.draw (node_nvml_power_watts)
- GPU utilization (%): nvml.utilization.gpu (node_nvml_utilization_percent)
- GPU memory utilization (%): nvml.memory.used_bytes / nvml.memory.total_bytes
- KV cache usage (tokens): redwood_runtime_kv_cache_tokens_total
- Inference qps and per-model tail latency (p50/p95/p99): redwood_requests_qps, redwood_latency_seconds{quantile=\"0.99\"}
- Ambient rack temperature (C): rack_ambient_temp_celsius (from rack sensors)
- Fan speeds / chassis thermal trip flags: chassis_fan_rpm, chassis_thermal_trip

Thresholds (operational defaults)
- Warning: GPU temp >= 80C for sustained 5m 
- Critical: GPU temp >= 85C for sustained 3m or any thermal_trip flag true
- Power margin low: available rack PSU margin < 10% for > 10m
- KV cache pressure: cache hit rate < 80% and memory utilization > 85%
- Latency SLO breach: p99 latency > 500ms for production routes for > 5m

Thermal management strategy
---------------------------
1) Tiered responses based on severity
   - Observe (warning): increase sampling, notify on-call, compute local forecast. No immediate throttle.
   - Mitigate (critical threshold): soft-evict low-priority background batches, reduce max_batch_size for affected workers, enable model-variant fallback to quantized model (if configured).
   - Protect (thermal_trip/unsafe): quiesce GPU: pause new inference requests, flush KV caches, perform controlled swap to regional fallback or Dedicated pool if available.

2) Hardware controls and integrations
   - redwood-agent exposes an HTTP control plane on localhost:4291 for graceful worker control (endpoints: /v1/worker/scale-down, /v1/worker/evict-tenants).
   - BMC/IPMI calls to increase fan curves when ambient exceeds 35C (see Appendix: ipmitool examples).
   - Integration with site BMS to adjust data center CRAC setpoints during fleet-wide heat events.

3) Cooling-aware scheduling
   - Scheduler labels nodes with thermal_score = f(ambient_temp, recent_power_draw, fan_health). Prefer cooler nodes for burst traffic.
   - Implement short-window heat-aware bin-packing to avoid concentrating heavy workloads on a single rack for extended periods.

Predictive capacity planner (24–72h)
------------------------------------
Overview:
- The planner is a lightweight service (redwood-capacity-predictor) that consumes metrics, calendar events (planned maintenance), and tenant growth signals to forecast headroom per rack and per-pool.
- Forecasting model: ensemble of exponential smoothing (ETS) for QPS and a gradient-boosted regression tree for thermal impact estimation.

Inputs:
- 1m QPS and token rate time-series for each tenant/model.
- Recent 6h power draw and temp trends.
- Scheduled jobs (nightly batch runs) from tenant manifests.
- Weather/ambient forecast (optional for exposed edge sites).

Outputs and actions:
- Hourly headroom reports (CSV/JSON) with columns: rack_id, forecasted_qps_peak, forecasted_gpu_temp_90pct, headroom_gpus, recommended_action.
- Automated tickets created in Jira (project RID-OPS) for predicted 'capacity risk' where headroom_gpus < 1 for peak windows.
- Recommended mitigations: pre-warm extra nodes, shift background retries to off-peak, enqueue cross-region fallback prepares.

Implementation steps (runbook for rolling out predictor)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Deploy redwood-capacity-predictor in staging with Prometheus and Thanos read access. Configure with role=staging and training window=14d.
2) Seed model with historical 90-day telemetry. Validate MAPE <= 12% on QPS and temp forecast on staging fleet.
3) Enable alerting: when predicted 95th percentile temp > 82C for any rack, create a P2 alert to ops.
4) Enable automated Jira ticketing for risk windows (optional toggle during pilot).
5) Run a 4-week pilot on 3 racks; keep manual overrides.

Operational runbook: immediate triage (on-call)
------------------------------------------------
When an alert fires (predicted temp exceedance or real-time thermal critical):
1) Triage (0–3 minutes)
   - Source: check alert in VictorOps/PagerDuty and open the rack dashboard (Grafana board: GPU-Thermal-Racks).
   - Confirm signals: node_nvml_temperature_celsius, chassis_fan_rpm, rack_ambient_temp_celsius.

2) Mitigate (3–15 minutes)
   - Call redwood-agent: POST http://localhost:4291/v1/worker/scale-down with body {\"target\":\"soft\"} on affected nodes.
   - Reduce worker max_batch_size: 
     curl -X POST http://localhost:4291/v1/config -d '{\"max_batch_size\":32}'
   - If fan RPM abnormal, file immediate hardware ticket with data center operator and increase fan curve via IPMI: ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0x66 0x01 0x00  (see vendor SOP)

3) Protect and failover (15–60 minutes)
   - If temps remain critical, execute tenant evictions for low-priority tenants: POST /v1/worker/evict-tenants {\"policy\":\"priority:low\",\"grace_seconds\":60}
   - Trigger model-variant fallback for production routes: set route override in redwood-controlplane to use quantized-model-v1 as fallback for affected nodes.
   - If no local headroom, initiate cross-region regional-failover playbook: follow private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 steps.

Recovery and post-incident
-------------------------
- After temps drop to warning levels for 15 minutes and p99 latencies are within SLO, incrementally bring evicted tenants back with a 10% QPS ramp every 2 minutes. Use the agent endpoint /v1/worker/resume-tenants.
- Record incident in postmortem with collected metrics: 30m window of nvml metrics, redwood-agent logs, and capacity predictor forecast.

Maintenance and preventive tasks
--------------------------------
- Weekly: run a fan-health diagnostic across all racks and record anomalies.
- Monthly: re-train forecasting model with latest 30–90 day telemetry.
- Quarterly: run a chaos drill simulating ambient heat spike and validate predictor and evictions.

KPIs, SLOs, and targets
------------------------
- Hardware safety: no GPU should exceed 90C at any time. (Hard objective)
- Latency SLO: p99 route latency <= 500ms 99% of time.
- Forecast accuracy: MAPE <= 15% for 24h QPS forecast, <= 12% for 24h temp forecast.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for thermal-critical alerts: <= 10 minutes.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary: Private Deployments Day2 Team (oncall rotation: pd-day2@redwood.internal).
- Secondary: Eng-SRE (for rack-level power/CRAC escalations).
- Hardware escalation: Data center operator and vendor field support if fan failures or thermal_trip flags persist after mitigations.

Appendix: Example Prometheus rules and Grafana panels
----------------------------------------------------
PromQL (sample alert rule):

ALERT GPUHighTempPredict
IF increase(node_nvml_temperature_celsius[5m]) > 0 and avg_over_time(node_nvml_temperature_celsius[10m]) > 82
FOR 3m
LABELS {severity=\"page\"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary=\"Predicted high GPU temp on {{ $labels.instance }}\"}

Grafana panels recommended:
- Rack thermal heatmap (x: time, y: rack_id, color: 95th pct temperature)
- Per-node power vs utilization scatter with ambient overlay
- Forecast horizon panel: predicted p99 temp with confidence band

Appendix: sample ipmitool / BMC command (vendor-specific)
- Increase fan curve (example vendor A): ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0x66 0x01 0x01
- Read chassis sensors: ipmitool sdr elist full

Appendix: sample redwood-agent control calls
- Soft scale-down:
  curl -X POST http://localhost:4291/v1/worker/scale-down -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"target\":\"soft\",\"reason\":\"thermal_mitigation\"}'
- Evict tenants:
  curl -X POST http://localhost:4291/v1/worker/evict-tenants -d '{\"policy\":\"priority:low\",\"grace_seconds\":60}'
